criteria.deficiency: The reference's public contract is Progress.open / Progress.wrap_file plus module-level open / wrap_file with mode, encoding, task_id and PathLike parameters. The candidate exposes only read(file, total, description) with str|BinaryIO input and no mode. This follows the PR-body text in the spec (which names Progress.read and rich.progress.read), so the naming is defensible against the spec, but it does not match the reference contract that the judge treats as the source of truth. Several reference-only tests (test_open, test_open_text_mode, test_wrap_file, test_wrap_file_task_total) call the reference names and would not be satisfied. Those tests are absent from the candidate, not deleted: patch.diff only adds to tests/test_progress.py.

Non-blocking note: the __getattr__ comment at generated/rich/progress.py:728-730 says name and mode are delegated, but typing.IO defines name and mode as properties that return None (typing.py:2521-2527 in the 3.10 stdlib I read; not verified against 3.9). The reference's _Reader inherits the same properties and has no __getattr__ (reference.diff:171-260), so reader.name and reader.mode return None in both. This is an inaccurate comment, not a reference regression.
criteria.deficiency: Non-blocking: the __getattr__ comment is inaccurate for name and mode, which resolve to typing.IO properties and return None rather than the wrapped handle's values. The reference behaves the same, so this is not a behavioral regression against it.

evidence: Docstrings use the Args/Returns/Raises format found in the repo (generated/rich/progress.py:158-220 and :983-1000, matching the track() docstring at original rich/progress.py:84-150).

The changelog entry is added under the existing Unreleased Added section (patch.diff:6-9). Test functions use -> None annotations and plain assert style (tests/test_progress.py:553-589), matching the file.

The spec's binary-reading intent is met: Progress.read accepts a path or file-like object (generated/rich/progress.py:982-1015), requires total for file-like objects with ValueError (:1009-1011), seek updates progress (:783-791), and read() is exposed as a context manager (:157-224).

Reference behavior that the candidate lacks: text-mode reading via open(file, "r"/"rt") wrapping in io.TextIOWrapper (reference.diff:688-696) and the reference test test_open_text_mode (reference test diff) asserting text reads. The candidate has no text-mode path; every reader it returns is binary (generated/rich/progress.py:1005, 1015).
The reference also reuses an existing task through task_id (reference.diff:571-589), which the candidate does not support.
criteria.deficiency: The candidate implements only the binary path that the PR-body spec describes. The reference, which the judge treats as the behavior source, also supports text-mode reading (mode r/rt, encoding, errors, newline, line buffering) and reuse of an existing task via task_id. The candidate supports none of these. The spec text itself describes only binary reads, so this is partly a gap between the spec and the reference, but the reference-level behavior is absent.
